proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV), electronically insulating phosphate that is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and LLZO. Its phosphate network should resist oxidation at 4 V vs Li and avoid strong interfacial reactions with the garnet, so it is a low-penalty buffer candidate.

Li3AlF6 is a wide-gap, Li-rich fluoride with high anodic stability, so it should resist oxidation by LiCoO2 at 4 V. Its Al-F bonds are strong, and it shares Li+ with LLZO, so it may avoid the La/Zr-driven decomposition seen for Li3PO4. This tests whether a halide-family coating gives a lower contact penalty than the phosphate.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with a wide gap, but its contact with LLZO released O2 and formed LaPO4 and ZrO2, giving penalty 0.099 eV/atom (bin 4, not acceptable). A different anion chemistry is needed to reduce that reaction.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap lithium zirconate oxide. Its Zr4+ and Li-O framework are chemically close to LLZO, so it should have fewer driving forces for La/Zr-redox-type contact reactions than the phosphate or fluoride coatings. It is also an established oxide coating chemistry for LiCoO2 at 4 V, so it should avoid the O2 release seen with Li3PO4 and Li3AlF6.
proposal.motivation: Both Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) and Li3AlF6 (mp-aaabfqnk) were insulating with wide gaps but gave identical LLZO contact penalties of about 0.099 eV/atom (bin 4), with O2 release and La/Zr-containing products. Changing to an oxide chemistry that shares Zr with the electrolyte may reduce that reaction.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, Li-rich orthoborate with B3+ that is hard to reduce and has no La or Zr to drive the LLZO reactions seen for Li3PO4 and Li2ZrO3. Its high lithium content should keep the interface close to LLZO's Li chemistry and limit O2 release at 4 V. This tests a borate family that has not been tried yet.
